claim_citation.quote: In *Green Lantern: War Journal #11*, by Phillip Kennedy Johnson, Montos, Adriano Lucas, and Dave Sharpe, John's conflict with the Old God called Olgrun and his Radiant Dead eventually leads him to come into possession of the Dark Star Ring, which grants the wielder greater power than any other ring in existence.

candidates.summary: John uses the Dark Star Ring to rebuild the long-destroyed Sacred Necropolis. This is a major full reconstruction feat, though it is a Dark Star Ring-assisted act rather than standard Green Lantern ring use.
candidates.title: Rebuilding the Sacred Necropolis
candidates.what_visibly_happens: The ruined Necropolis is rebuilt on-page as John reshapes the structure into a functional place that traps Olgrun and his realm inside.

candidates.character_or_thing: John Stewart re-creates destroyed city buildings with his ring

claim_citation.quote: The alternate Green Lantern immediately re-creates the old ghetto buildings, repairing them in the process.

candidates.summary: Direct, full construct feat: John repairs an entire destroyed block/buildings on-page. This is a straightforward utility construct, not an assisted or temporary illusion.
candidates.title: Rebuilding the destroyed city block
candidates.what_visibly_happens: After the Key’s attack destroys buildings, John immediately remakes the ruined structures with his ring so the block is restored.

candidates.character_or_thing: John Stewart creates a group of Marines as combat constructs

claim_citation.quote: John then uses his power to create a group of Marines, who fight alongside him against the Black Lanterns.

candidates.summary: Full construct feat: John manifests a squad of Marine constructs to fight with him. This is a tactical/assisted battlefield use of the ring rather than a permanent creation.
candidates.title: Blackest Night Marine squad
candidates.what_visibly_happens: John summons a whole Marine unit that joins the fight against the Black Lanterns.

candidates.character_or_thing: John Stewart fires a sniper-rifle construct into Mogo’s core

claim_citation.quote: John constructs a sniper rifle and fires a bullet into Mogo's core, killing the living planet and stopping the creation of corrupted rings.

candidates.summary: Full construct feat: John builds a precise sniper rifle construct and uses it to deliver the finishing shot that kills Mogo. This is one of his most lethal and technically detailed constructs.
candidates.title: The Mogo sniper shot
candidates.what_visibly_happens: John manifests a sniper rifle, takes aim, and shoots a bullet straight into Mogo’s core.

candidates.character_or_thing: John Stewart creates a construct of his dead sister Ellie

claim_citation.quote: I do appreciate the stuff with his mom at the start and how he pushed himself to go further and really test the limit of what he can 'build' but I think it could have been done in fewer pages. Great art, the last 4 pages are where it really pops. Well that and when he makes his sister.

candidates.summary: Temporary/autonomous construct feat: John makes a sister construct, which commenters describe as an emotionally loaded, semi-living build. This is more advanced than a simple object construct because it is meant to function like a person.
candidates.title: Ellie sister construct
candidates.what_visibly_happens: John builds a construct of his sister, and the issue highlights that page as one of the standout moments.

candidates.character_or_thing: John Stewart’s construct sister Ellie merged with Shirley Stewart

claim_citation.quote: Green Lantern: War Journal #12 is an issue of the series Green Lantern: War Journal (Volume 1) with a cover date of October, 2024.

candidates.summary: Persistent/merged construct feat: John’s sister construct is still present and is explicitly listed as merged with Shirley Stewart. This is the most extreme version of the construct idea in the reviewed material because it blends a construct with a deceased loved one’s presence.
candidates.title: Ellie/Shirley construct-merger
candidates.what_visibly_happens: The construct version of Ellie is still active, and the issue page identifies Ellie Stewart’s construct as merged with Shirley Stewart.
